description: Example V0.4.0 venue session. Three streams from two cameras, deliberately heterogeneous: different frame rates, different start times and different durations, because a real venue's existing CCTV is never uniform. Nothing here describes a layout, an overlap or a coverage area — Atreides never assumes camera geometry, and non-overlapping cameras are an ordinary case. 'cam_north' stopped and restarted during the session, so it has two sources; their position in the list is the stream epoch, and crossing that boundary breaks track identity: (cam_north, track_7) before and after are unrelated tracklets. A camera with several sources must declare where each one starts, and a declared 'start_offset_seconds' always carries an 'offset_accuracy_seconds' — an offset with no stated accuracy would be read as exact, which no manually declared offset is. 'cam_west' declares neither, which is fully supported: it starts at venue zero with its alignment NOT_ESTABLISHED. 'declared_fps' overrides a container that reports a frame rate it does not have; every source-relative timestamp is derived from that number, so it is recorded as an operator statement rather than passed off as the container's own. The paths below are examples: data/input/ is git-ignored and nothing is downloaded.
